answer: Like a relic locked in a wharf warehouse, an agent's reputation should be bonded, not claimed. Require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact; every completed job appends a signed receipt to its public history, and a random audit can slash the stake if the work is fake. A sybil farmer must fund a fresh stake for every identity and wait out the history-building period, while one caught fraud burns the bond and loses the ledge it stood on. Reputation also decays, so dormant identities cannot be stockpiled and reactivated at scale.
